subject: ipsupport-code
title: Embedded offline-trained linear risk classifier scores every tool call in shadow mode by default, logging disagreements with the permission policy while blocking nothing
one_why: Unlike gptme's deterministic shadow guardrail, the scorer is a real 768KB SGD model trained offline (stdlib-only Python, byte-reproducible, embedded via go:embed), on unless IPS_RISK=off because 'a signal nobody enables collects none'; per-workspace learned delta corrections live beside project state and are dropped if they no longer match the base model's positional labels; end-of-session stats line reports calls/flagged/disagreed so promotion to enforcement is a data decision, not a vibe decision.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Monthly model-retrain CI refuses to open its own PR if held-out precision/recall regresses >0.05, with cross-language feature parity pinned by shared hash constants
one_why: The whole ML loop is offline and deterministic (vendored vocab, fixed python pin so 'byte-identical model.bin' is meaningful), the feature extractor is duplicated in Python and Go purely so no runtime dep ships, and the duplication is guarded both ways: HASH_VECTORS asserted against Go-produced values in the trainer, pinned again in Go tests; the refresh job can only propose - an automated retrain that can merge itself will one day ship a worse model.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Reflection-distilled pitfalls injected into tool-error results on error-pattern match, with a distinct 'avoid' kind for dead ends and generic-pattern guards
one_why: Lessons are keyed (domain, error-pattern) and surface only in the failed tool result they match - not the system prompt - so a weak model isn't buried; a dead-end lesson renders differently ('this never works') because telling a model 'this worked: the thing that never worked' is worse than silence; five spec tests pin that hints never present a dead end as a fix, never cross actions sharing error text, and never surface generic 'exit N' patterns; age-based pruning via LastSeen keeps the store fresh.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: One-sample calibration of the 4-bytes/token estimate against the server's prompt_tokens measured on the as-sent request, clamped 0.5-4, with a trim pass that preserves the failure-signal lines
one_why: Nuance on mocode's usage-feedback trigger: instead of an EWMA, a single clamped ratio from the just-sent turn corrects the estimate, deliberately computed on messages-as-sent because dividing an old reading by the now-larger estimate produced a sub-1 ratio that shrank the number it was meant to correct (documented live blowout: 32.8k window went 5k->20k->44k because HTML tokenizes at half assumed density); trimming also keeps the exit-status + reason lines so mid-task trims don't erase the failure signal the lesson store later keys off.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Compaction keeps a deterministic verbatim actions-digest alongside the LLM prose recap, re-harvested by a shared marker so it survives N successive compactions
one_why: Caught live: a weak model's prose summary blurred 'go.mod already exists' and the next task re-ran the exact command that had always failed; so file-touch/command/failure records are appended after the model answers - no user focus steer can drop them - and the digest block is written with the same marker the next Compact's reader scans for, making the audit trail idempotent across repeated compaction; the FAILED-entry wording also warns against re-running unchanged while explicitly NOT forbidding re-verification after a fix.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Hard floor is argv-aware and wrapper-transparent; allow-globs require every chained segment to match and refuse command substitution and redirections; deny-globs re-checked after async approval
one_why: Beyond glob matching: 'xargs rm -rf' and 'env FOO=1 rm -rf' hit the floor because it looks through wrappers and is reorder-proof on recursive flags; an allow-glob never spans && chains (git * can't smuggle a second command), never auto-allows $(), backticks or redirections whose target the glob can't see; DeniedWrite is re-run against the freshly re-resolved path after an approval wait closes a symlink-swap TOCTOU; the secret-read floor (.env, *secret*) can't be disabled by config, and the jail chases dangling symlink targets with a chain-depth limit (tested).

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Goal ends only on explicit DONE, TTL expiry, or the user: judge verdicts of 'unclear' re-feed rather than end, and every give-up path (turn failure, stuck-stop, step exhaustion) gets a judge pass with a persisted gap note for resume
one_why: 'Silence is not acceptance' - a judge that can't answer (its own reasoning ate the output budget) had silently abandoned a goal with 254/255 returns unspent; the fix makes judgeDone the sole early terminator, treats unclear as more, and runs judgeOnGiveUp on all three give-up paths fed by a deterministic actionsDigest because the isolated judge call never sees the transcript; the judge's 'still missing' text persists into the standing goal with the run's Progressed flag so a later /goal go resumes with a real hint instead of amnesia.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Per-turn file+history checkpoints with unified-diff revert preview, but session-lifetime in-memory only - a crash loses all rewind state
one_why: Preview-before-revert is the good part: the picker shows per-file restore/delete/toobig deltas plus the conversation-trim count computed against the checkpoint's history length; but unlike cline's git-stash checkpoints (anchor 8) nothing is persisted, and external-CLI sub-agent edits are explicitly outside rewind's view - honestly documented rather than silently missed.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Clean loop/product split undermined by cmd/agent/main.go at 5,981 LOC plus tui.go at 3,375 (and main_test.go at 9,469)
one_why: Per the pi errata a >5k product-mode file docks architecture on both sides: the testable core (internal/agent over an interface) is genuinely well separated, but wiring, sessions, spawn planning, risk hookup, config commands and flags share one file, and the matching test god-file signals the same coupling at the test surface.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Kernel write-jail (Seatbelt / Landlock re-exec shim that fails CLOSED) sits under the policy engine and is tested on a real macOS runner - but ships default-off and auto-mode runs unconfined with only a warning
one_why: Landlock restricts the calling process, so the wrapper re-execs the agent binary with a hidden __landlock-exec argv and self-confines before exec'ing the real command - and if the kernel probe misses on that leg it exits 126 rather than running free; network deny is ABI-gated with the offline flag as the primary gate; the docking point is the default: sandbox='off', and on kernels without Landlock, 'auto' logs a warn and runs unconfined, so containment-under-approval is opt-in.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Whole-binary and whole-TUI e2e against httptest fake OpenAI providers, including a session-persist-across-restart test driven through teatest
one_why: Nuance on the seeded id: not just scripted chats at unit level - TestE2E_Binary builds and drives the real binary end-to-end, and the TUI specs assert stream rendering, no-race semantics between config reload/MCP connect and concurrent UI reads, and that the context meter reads the agent's main-turn figure rather than a side call's - UI and loop paths are covered, which the nanocoder anchor's 7 was docked for lacking.
